title: Adam's grace and Christ's grace
source_text: V. Caeterum gratia illa naturae opposita a nonnullis Scholae Romanae Doctoribus sedulo distinguitur in eam quae homini ante lapsum collata est, & eam quae homini lapso per meritum Christi confertur. Ac priorem illam gratiam vocant, gratiam Adami: Posteriorem vero gratiam Christi. Prior ab illis dicitur gratia sanitatis: haec vero posterior gratia Medicinalis. Prior collata est homini non merenti: posterior etiam indigno.
pass_a_gloss: V. But that grace opposed to nature is by some Doctors of the Roman School carefully distinguished into that which was conferred on man before the fall, and that which is conferred on man fallen through the merit of Christ. And that former grace they call the grace of Adam: but the latter the grace of Christ. The former is called by them the grace of health: but this latter the Medicinal grace. The former was conferred on man not meriting: the latter even on one unworthy.
pass_b_english: Thesis V. Some doctors of the Roman School take care to divide this grace that is set against nature into two: the grace given to man before the fall, and the grace given to fallen man through Christ's merit.

They call the first the grace of Adam and the second the grace of Christ; the first the grace of health and the second healing grace. The first was given to a man who had not earned it, the second to one who was actually unworthy of it.
